series.interpretation: Within-country nominal income history. Household-size equivalisation differs from per-person survey values. National currencies are not ranked across countries.

series.label: Household consumption price level, United States = 100
series.unit: index, United States = 100 in the same year
series.definition: Published spatial household-consumption price level; a broad price context, not a household-specific minimum living-cost budget.
series.adjustment: Published national index; source estimation and compilation methods retained
series.source_name: Price level index (Households and NPISHs Final consumption expenditure)
series.source_note: The price level index (PLI) is the ratio of a purchasing power parity (PPP) conversion factor to the corresponding market exchange rate between two countries, expressed relative to a base country that is set equal to 100. For this series the base country is the United States. It provides a measure of the differences in price level between the country and the United States by indicating the number of units of the common currency (US dollars) needed to buy the same volume of the aggregation level in each country. This indicator provides a measure of the differences in the price levels of countries at the level of Households and NPISHs final consumption expenditure.
series.source_organization: World Development Indicators, World Bank (WB), uri: https://databank.worldbank.org/source/world-development-indicators, publisher: World Development Indicators
series.estimate_note: Published official/compiled estimate; an empty observation-status field does not certify direct measurement.
series.interpretation: Consumer price-level context relative to the United States in the same year: 80 means a broad household-consumption price level about 20% below the U.S. reference. Changes reflect relative prices and exchange rates, not national inflation alone.

series.label: Consumer price index, national 2010 = 100
series.definition: Within-country consumer price history. National CPI index levels cannot rank cost of living across countries.
series.adjustment: Published national index; source estimation and compilation methods retained
series.source_note: Index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period (2010=100).
series.source_organization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)
series.estimate_note: Published official/compiled estimate; an empty observation-status field does not certify direct measurement.
series.interpretation: National consumer-price change over time, 2010 = 100. Index levels do not rank living costs across countries.

series.label: Household consumption per person, constant 2021 PPP
series.definition: Calculated national-account consumption total divided by the same country’s population in the same year. Includes nonprofits serving households; not a median household budget or household income.
series.adjustment: Calculated per-person estimate from published constant-2021 PPP consumption and population
series.estimate_note: Calculated from published estimates; no interpolation or extrapolation.
series.interpretation: National-account household and nonprofit-institution consumption divided by same-year total population. This is an average, including consumption such as imputed housing services, not a median cash budget.

series.label: Consumer price change, national 2021 = 100
series.definition: National CPI rebased to 2021 = 100 using this country’s published 2021 CPI. Levels remain unsuitable for cross-country price comparisons.
series.estimate_note: Calculated from published estimates; no interpolation or extrapolation.
series.interpretation: National CPI divided by that country’s 2021 CPI, multiplied by 100. A value of 110 indicates prices about 10% above that country’s 2021 level; it is not a cross-country cost ranking.

series.name: Median equivalised disposable household income
series.definition: Annual disposable household income, equivalised by the square root of household size and attributed to household members; entire population. Current definition, income methodology since 2012.
series.unit: 2021 national currency per equivalent household member per year
series.price_basis: Calculated national CPI adjustment to that country’s 2021 prices
series.cross_country_comparison: Not directly comparable across currencies; no PPP conversion applied locally
series.temporal_comparison: Nominal only until country-specific price adjustment; current definition and METH2012 retained separately from older methods
series.label: Median disposable household income, national 2021 prices
series.native_definition: Annual disposable household income, equivalised by the square root of household size and attributed to household members; entire population. Current definition, income methodology since 2012.
series.adjustment: Analyst-calculated estimate: original income × country CPI(2021) / country CPI(income year)
series.interpretation: Within-country inflation-adjusted equivalised disposable income. Retain the record currency code and source definition. Different national currencies remain separate; no GDP or consumption PPP factor is applied to this income series.

sources.title: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform
OECD income rebased using the same country’s published CPI

limitations: National averages, survey medians, equivalised disposable income, consumer price levels and inflation indices retain different concepts and denominators; they are not combined into a household budget or universal affordability score.

Published survey, national-account and PPP/index values are estimates or compiled statistics. Blank native status fields do not certify direct measurement; original flags, footnotes and source methods remain available.

PIP uses native reporting years for maps and exact survey years in source context. Survey comparability spells and welfare types remain distinct. No missing survey years are interpolated or carried forward locally.
Published constant-2021 PPP income and consumption values are not adjusted again. Local derived estimates identify all inputs and formulas.
Price-level indices compare countries against the United States in each year; national CPI index levels support within-country price change and cannot rank countries by living costs.
OECD original and CPI-adjusted income retain national currencies, equivalisation and methodology. National currencies are not compared as equal units across countries.
Consumption includes nonprofit institutions serving households and national-account imputations. It measures consumption, not necessarily out-of-pocket cash expenditure.
These are source-attached household research covariates. No industry demand shock is automatically translated into household income, prices, inequality or welfare effects.
Exact country/reporting-year joins only. Missing values, unmatched countries and rest-of-world remain unavailable; no GDP-per-person household substitute is supplied.
Consumption national accounts include nonprofit institutions serving households (NPISHs). Consumption is not income and per-person means do not describe a typical household or inequality.
Constant 2021 PPP consumption is already price-adjusted; no U.S. GDP deflator is applied.

Household-consumption price-level index compares broad national prices with United States = 100 in each year. It is not a local housing quotation, household-specific basket or minimum living-cost estimate.
CPI measures within-country price change. Rebasing cannot make national CPI levels comparable price levels across countries.
Blank native observation flags do not rule out source estimation. Native missing values, original flags, footnotes and source rows are retained.
No interpolation, nearest-year filling, unsupported territory substitution or original-source rewriting is performed.
Current local-currency consumption values require a valid country, currency and period context. They are not directly comparable across countries.
PPP factor and exchange-rate sources are retained for audit; the published native PLI is used rather than a local PPP/FX substitution.
PIP income and consumption are distinct welfare measures and must not be silently combined into a single income series.
PIP mean and median are daily household welfare per capita, while OECD income is annual equivalised disposable income; their denominators and definitions differ.
PIP values have already been CPI/PPP adjusted by the source. No local inflation or PPP conversion is applied.
All PIP displayed rows are national survey estimates with fill_gaps=false and is_interpolated=false. Missing annual survey data remain unavailable.
Use native reporting_year for annual views and preserve exact survey_year. Tanzania's 2018 reporting year has survey_year 2017.92; flooring would silently change its source period.

A PIP comparable_spell and survey_comparability code identify a source-defined series segment, not universal cross-country equivalence. Do not fit a continuous temporal trend across a break without an explicit research decision.
OECD current-definition METH2012 rows are selected without stitching to older methods. Earlier/previous definitions remain available in the original CSV and exclusion ledger.
OECD national-currency income values are nominal and require country-specific CPI and suitable consumption PPP/currency checks for comparable real purchasing-power reporting.
The OECD normal-value flag is not a claim that survey uncertainty is absent. Provisional flags remain explicit.
Neither source is a quoted household necessities basket or a complete household affordability budget; housing, wealth, public services and household composition remain relevant.
